selected_evidence.requirement: AIDE installed and configured to monitor /etc with content-level integrity checks
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed Ubuntu 16.04 node1, installed aide/aide-common, and confirmed via aide.conf.d that /etc is monitored recursively with full checksums (SHA256/SHA512/etc.) via the top-level '/ Full' rule, with only known-volatile files (resolv.conf, adjtime, etc.) exempted.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline database initialized and in place at the configured active path
selected_evidence.summary: Ran aideinit; produced /var/lib/aide/aide.db with 70,149 entries; confirmed aide.db and aide.db.new have identical md5sums, i.e. the baseline is correctly installed as the active database.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline correctly reflects a clean, healthy /etc state (no false positives)
selected_evidence.summary: Ran aide --check immediately after init; found differences only in ephemeral /run and /var/lib/lxcfs session/cgroup pseudo-files (created by our own SSH-like exec sessions), with zero differences under /etc/ (grep -c "/etc/" returned 0).

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline detects and reports later changes to files in /etc (core task requirement)
selected_evidence.summary: Appended a marker line to /etc/hosts, ran aide.wrapper --check, and confirmed AIDE reported /etc/hosts as changed with detailed size/mtime/ctime/SHA256/SHA512/RMD160/TIGER/HAVAL/GOST/CRC32 before/after values, proving detection and reporting works.

selected_evidence.requirement: Automated ongoing reporting mechanism exists (later changes can be 'reported')
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed /etc/cron.daily/aide exists (from aide-common package) which runs aide --check daily and reports differences automatically.

selected_evidence.requirement: Restore system to clean baseline state after the detection demonstration
selected_evidence.summary: Restored /etc/hosts to original content and re-ran aideinit to rebuild the baseline database reflecting the clean, restored state.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline captured before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (a1dc8e25-9492-4e80-81a5-6337330a5f77) and ran aide.wrapper --check pre-restart, confirming zero differences under real /etc paths (only /run and lxcfs session churn).

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnection, and node polled back online
selected_evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded `sudo reboot`; acknowledgement returned; subsequent exec confirmed connection refused (node down); later exec succeeded confirming node1 back online.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proven (not just uptime)
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 2e616fe5-1dc9-466c-a901-f588c73a88dd, differing from the pre-restart value a1dc8e25-9492-4e80-81a5-6337330a5f77, proving an actual reboot occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required data/service verified
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed AIDE database file intact post-restart (identical md5sum to pre-restart), cron.service active, and a fresh aide --check post-restart showed zero real /etc/ differences (the only /etc/-matching diffs were postfix chroot copies under /var/spool/postfix/etc, refreshed on boot, not actual /etc files).

# AIDE conf

# The daily cron job depends on these paths
database=file:/var/lib/aide/aide.db
database_out=file:/var/lib/aide/aide.db.new
database_new=file:/var/lib/aide/aide.db.new
gzip_dbout=yes

# Set to no to disable summarize_changes option.
summarize_changes=yes

# Set to no to disable grouping of files in report.
grouped=yes

# standard verbose level
verbose = 6

# Set to yes to print the checksums in the report in hex format
report_base16 = no

# if you want to sacrifice security for speed, remove some of these
# checksums. Whirlpool is broken on sparc and sparc64 (see #429180,
# #420547, #152203).
Checksums = sha256+sha512+rmd160+haval+gost+crc32+tiger

# The checksums of the databases to be printed in the report
# Set to 'E' to disable.
database_attrs = Checksums

# check permissions, owner, group and file type
OwnerMode = p+u+g+ftype

# Check size and block count
Size = s+b

# Files that stay static
InodeData = OwnerMode+n+i+Size+l+X
StaticFile = m+c+Checksums

# Files that stay static but are copied to a ram disk on startup
# (causing different inode)
RamdiskData = InodeData-i

# Check everything
Full = InodeData+StaticFile

# Files that change their mtimes or ctimes but not their contents
VarTime = InodeData+Checksums

# Files that are recreated regularly but do not change their contents
VarInode = VarTime-i

# Files that change their contents during system operation
VarFile = OwnerMode+n+l+X

# Directories that change their contents during system operation
VarDir = OwnerMode+n+i+X

# Directories that are recreated regularly and change their contents
VarDirInode = OwnerMode+n+X
